articles.excerpt: Speaking on JioStar, Cheteshwar Pujara says Kohli's No. 3 anchor role gives him the edge over Rohit Sharma, and India's split squad points to a drawn series.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans in New Zealand and elsewhere, the five-match ODI series runs November 4 to 15, 2026 across Auckland, Mount Maunganui, Hamilton and Wellington.

articles.title: Hardik Pandya Set for Punjab Kings Move in Arshdeep Swap, Reports Say
articles.excerpt: Sportstar reports, via Sportskeeda and CricTracker, that Mumbai and Punjab have all but agreed a Pandya-for-Arshdeep and Vishnu Vinod exchange — unconfirmed by either franchise or the IPL.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora IPL fans, the reported Pandya-Arshdeep swap is unconfirmed until a franchise or IPL announcement, expected in reports before the November 17 retention deadline.

articles.title: T20's Arms Race: Fearless Batters, and Bowlers Learning to Think a Step Ahead
articles.excerpt: An ESPNcricinfo analysis of the India-New Zealand series argues the format is mutating ball by ball — batters have abandoned fear, and bowlers are answering with deception and a new way of judging themselves. R Ashwin is not convinced India's attack is keeping up.
articles.nri_angle: India's T20 evolution is the format diaspora fans watch most; the series underlines why India's fearless batting travels well while its Bumrah-less bowling remains the open question.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hardik Pandya to Return via Domestic Cricket, Shubman Gill Says
articles.excerpt: The injured all-rounder, rehabilitating in Bengaluru since June after quad and shin injuries, must prove his fitness in domestic cricket before an India comeback, his captain confirmed.
articles.nri_angle: Pandya's fitness is a central question for India fans in the diaspora following the New Zealand ODI series and the build-up to the ODI World Cup.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India-Pakistan World Cup Clash Draws 8.4 Million Ticket Requests as Ballot Tops 120 Million
articles.excerpt: The October 10, 2027 match at the Wanderers has 8,397,294 applications for a 34,000-seat stadium. The free ballot closes on November 21 — fans who miss it cannot buy through the ballot at all.
articles.image_caption: The headquarters of the International Cricket Council. The ICC said ticket requests for the 2027 Men's Cricket World Cup passed 120 million, with the India-Pakistan match drawing 8,397,294 requests.
articles.nri_angle: The United States is among the top five countries registering for the ballot, alongside South Africa, the UK, India and Australia; US-based fans have until 23:59 CAT on November 21 to enter free at tickets.cricketworldcup.com.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Glenn Maxwell Retires From International Cricket, Ending 286-Match Australia Career
articles.excerpt: The 38-year-old all-rounder, a three-time World Cup winner, will keep playing T20 franchise cricket for Melbourne Stars after calling time on internationals, first-class and List A cricket.
articles.image_caption: Australia's Glenn Maxwell celebrates during a T20 international match. Maxwell announced his retirement from international cricket, ending a 286-match career for Australia.
articles.nri_angle: Maxwell's five T20I centuries, a record he shares with India's Rohit Sharma, and his 201 not out against Afghanistan in 2023 made him a familiar figure to Indian and diaspora audiences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India in New Zealand: Kohli Needs Four Runs to Reach 600 as ODI Series Opens Wednesday
articles.excerpt: Kohli's 596 ODI runs in New Zealand leave him two behind Sehwag and chasing Tendulkar's 821, as India return for five ODIs after losing the home series to the Black Caps in January.
articles.nri_angle: A five-match ODI series in New Zealand prime time is appointment viewing for the diaspora across Australasia, North America and the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ravindra and Chapman Ruled Out of New Zealand's ODI Series Against India
articles.excerpt: A hamstring that needs two more weeks and a shoulder injured in a promo shoot leave the hosts without two first-choice batters for all five ODIs against India, starting Wednesday in Auckland.
articles.nri_angle: India's ODI tour of New Zealand loses two of the hosts' biggest names before the first ball in Auckland, reshaping the series for the diaspora fans following it.

articles.title: Sindhu and Lakshya Sen Complete an Indian Double at the Hylo Open
articles.excerpt: Sindhu beat Kjaersfeldt 21-12, 21-14 and Sen beat defending champion Christie 21-17, 21-10 as India took both singles titles at the Super 500 event in Saarbrücken.
articles.image_caption: P. V. Sindhu stands on the podium with her gold medal at the Hylo Open in Saarbrücken. Sindhu beat Denmark's Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt in straight games to become the first Indian woman to win the tournament.
articles.nri_angle: Two of India's most followed shuttlers winning on the same European Sunday gives diaspora badminton fans a rare double to celebrate.

articles.title: One Year On: The Night India's Women Won the World Cup and Changed the Game
articles.excerpt: On November 2, 2025, India beat South Africa by 52 runs in Navi Mumbai for a first ICC title. A year later, the endorsements have transformed — the T20 crown is still missing.
articles.image_caption: India's women's team celebrates with the World Cup trophy after the 2025 final. India beat South Africa by 52 runs at DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai, to win their first ICC title.
articles.nri_angle: The 2025 title remains the reference point for Indian families abroad putting daughters into cricket — and its endorsement surge is the business story that followed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rishabh Pant Ruled Out of Final India A Match, Doubtful for Wellington Test
articles.excerpt: Pant will miss the November 7 India A match in Lincoln with a left-side strain, and his place in the first Test against New Zealand on November 19 depends on a fitness evaluation that has no confirmed timeline.
articles.image_caption: Rishabh Pant batting for India against England. Pant will miss India A's final match against New Zealand A in Lincoln as he recovers from a left-side strain, and is doubtful for the Wellington Test.

articles.title: India Beat Sri Lanka and Uganda to Complete Commonwealth Kabaddi Double
articles.excerpt: India won the men's final 54-20 over Sri Lanka and the women's final 35-15 over Uganda in Ahmedabad to claim both titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship.
articles.image_caption: India and Uganda players feature on the Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026 highlights graphic from Ahmedabad. India won both the men's and women's titles at the championship.
articles.nri_angle: India's double title in a home-grown sport at its first Commonwealth championship gives diaspora kabaddi fans a clear marker of the game's growing international footprint.

articles.title: Kuldeep and Varun Stay Benched as India Weigh Hamilton Call for Final T20I
articles.excerpt: Neither wrist-spinner has played a game in the New Zealand series. Spin coach Sairaj Bahutule says the Hamilton XI will be decided only after a look at the pitch — and both men are ready if called.
articles.image_caption: Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy walk together in India training kit. Neither wrist-spinner has featured in the New Zealand T20I series, and the Hamilton playing XI will be decided after a pitch inspection.
articles.nri_angle: The five-match ODI series that follows the Hamilton T20I is where Kuldeep, who is in the ODI squad, is likeliest to return.

articles.title: India-Born Jai Moondra Takes Record 6 for 26 as Ireland Level Namibia Series
articles.excerpt: Moondra's six-wicket haul bowled Namibia out for 168 as Ireland won the fourth ODI by 130 runs to set up a Sunday decider at 2-2.
articles.nri_angle: India-born Ireland seamer Jai Moondra set a national ODI bowling record in the series-levelling win.

articles.title: Prasidh Krishna Ruled Out of New Zealand ODI Series
articles.excerpt: The BCCI says Prasidh Krishna needs more time to build match workload as he recovers from a hamstring injury, while Mohammed Siraj joins India A for the second four-day game against New Zealand A.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans planning to follow or attend India's New Zealand tour, the update reshapes the pace attack for the ODI series opening November 4 in Auckland.

articles.title: Yuvraj Singh Says India Must Give Young Batters ODI Chances
articles.excerpt: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh says leaving Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi out of 50-over cricket does not do justice to their talent, while conceding competition for places is fierce.
articles.image_caption: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh (file photo)
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora cricket fans following India's New Zealand tour, Yuvraj's intervention frames the selection debate they will watch through the ODI series starting November 4 in Auckland.

articles.title: Phillips' 107 Powers New Zealand to Record 259/7 and 87-Run Win Over India
articles.excerpt: Glenn Phillips smashed 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell 65 off 25 as New Zealand posted their highest-ever T20I total — and the highest against India — before Jacob Duffy's 4/23 sealed an 87-run win in the fourth T20I at Eden Park. India still lead the series 3-1.
articles.nri_angle: India's first defeat of the series came in front of a sold-out Eden Park crowd with a large Indian diaspora presence; the fifth and final T20I now decides whether India close the tour 4-1 or 3-2.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sold-Out Eden Park Crowd to Break New Zealand Bilateral Record for India T20I
articles.excerpt: Nearly 40,000 fans will watch Friday's fourth T20I in Auckland, passing the 36,523 mark set in 2019 — for a series India have already won.
articles.image_caption: Beautiful panorama of Eden Park stadium in Auckland, New Zealand, photographed by Kiwi Flickr. Friday's fourth T20I between New Zealand and India at Eden Park is sold out, with nearly 40,000 fans expected in Auckland.
articles.image_credit: Photo: This image's author is Kiwi Flickr Attribution — You must give appropriate credi via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
articles.nri_angle: A record Eden Park crowd for an India match shows the diaspora-driven commercial pull of Indian cricket in New Zealand.

articles.title: Josh Inglis Makes Australian History With Comeback Test Century in Cape Town Decider
articles.excerpt: Recalled at short notice after a finger injury, Inglis scored 102 off 135 balls against South Africa at Newlands to become the first Australian with multiple centuries in all three international formats.
articles.image_caption: Josh Inglis raises his bat and helmet to celebrate his century against South Africa at Newlands in Cape Town. His 102 made him the first Australian with multiple centuries in all three international formats.
articles.nri_angle: Indian fans know Inglis from the IPL — Punjab Kings signed him for Rs 2.60 crore in 2025 and Lucknow Super Giants paid Rs 8.6 crore for him at the IPL 2026 mini-auction.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At 15, Uma Kashvi Becomes Youngest Player Ever Signed in WPL Auction
articles.excerpt: Delhi Capitals bought the Karnataka all-rounder for Rs 10 lakh in Kochi — 15 years and 202 days old, with an Under-15 average of 172 behind her.
articles.nri_angle: The WPL's youngest signing is a window on how early India's women's cricket pipeline now identifies and contracts talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UP Warriorz Sign Sophie Molineux for Rs 1.10 Crore at WPL Auction
articles.excerpt: Australia's captain was the costliest buy in Kochi as UP Warriorz filled all eight open slots, brought back Grace Harris, and beat RCB in the day's biggest bidding contest.
articles.image_caption: Australian cricketer Sophie Molineux, signed by UP Warriorz for Rs 1.10 crore at the WPL auction
articles.nri_angle: The WPL auction shapes the squads Indian and diaspora cricket fans will follow when the league's fifth season starts in January.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pramanik's Eight Wickets Put Bengal Six Wickets From Third Straight Ranji Win
articles.excerpt: Left-arm spinner Pradipta Pramanik took four wickets in each innings as Bengal bowled Kerala out for 141, set a target of 409 and reduced the hosts to 53 for 4 by the close of day three in Thiruvananthapuram.
articles.nri_angle: Ranji Trophy form from players such as Mohammed Shami shapes India's Test selection debates followed closely by diaspora cricket fans.

articles.title: Arshdeep Singh Breaks Bhuvneshwar Record With 38 T20I Wickets in 2026
articles.excerpt: The left-arm seamer's 2 for 33 against New Zealand in Christchurch took him past Bhuvneshwar Kumar's 37 wickets in 2022, in 26 innings, and level with Wanindu Hasaranga in the full-member list.
articles.image_caption: Arshdeep Singh playing for India at the MCG during the 2022 T20 World Cup (Wikimedia Commons).
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans following India's New Zealand tour, Arshdeep's next matches carry a second storyline: two more wickets would make him the outright full-member record holder for T20I wickets in a calendar year.

articles.title: Ashes and India Series Power Cricket Australia to Record A$601 Million Revenue
articles.excerpt: A home Ashes and India's white-ball tour turned an A$11.3 million loss into an A$81.8 million surplus, even as two-day Tests cost CA A$20 million and lean years loom.
articles.image_caption: Australian players celebrate a wicket during a Test match. Cricket Australia reported record revenue of A$601.1 million and an A$81.8 million surplus for 2025-26, driven by the Ashes and India's white-ball tour.
articles.nri_angle: India's white-ball tour was one of the two properties that produced Cricket Australia's record year, underlining the commercial weight Indian and diaspora audiences carry in world cricket.
